classification_notes.methodology: Each request classified based on primary intent using linguistic patterns and context. When requests contained multiple intents, the dominant action verb or primary outcome determined classification.
challenges: Backup-related requests (req-094 to req-100) don't map to any of the 8 categories directly. Most classified as 'deploy' for deploying backup infrastructure, 'audit' for verification, or 'security' for data protection.
Migration requests (req-125 to req-135) classified as 'deploy' since they involve deploying new infrastructure/databases.
Update/upgrade requests (req-101 to req-104) classified as 'deploy' since they involve deploying new versions.
Configuration setup requests classified as 'deploy' when they're setting up new infrastructure for deployment.
Questions asking 'show me' or 'display' classified as 'monitor' since they're requesting monitoring data.
Restart-related issues classified as 'diagnose' when they indicate problems, 'deploy' when they're about deployment mechanisms.
corrections_from_preliminary: req-075 to req-084: Preliminary intent was 'configure' (not in 8 categories), reclassified mostly to 'deploy'
req-094 to req-100: Preliminary intent was 'backup' (not in 8 categories), reclassified to 'deploy', 'audit', or 'security'
req-101 to req-104: Preliminary intent was 'update' (not in 8 categories), reclassified to 'deploy'
req-125 to req-135: Preliminary intent was 'migrate' (not in 8 categories), reclassified mostly to 'deploy' or 'diagnose'
req-027: Changed from 'rollback' to 'diagnose' since rollback already happened and investigation is needed
req-043: Kept as 'cost' though multi-factor since cost is explicitly mentioned
high_confidence_patterns: Questions starting with 'Why is X slow' → always diagnose (100% confidence)
'how much are we spending' → always cost (98%+ confidence)
